memory_update.text: POWL should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a high-relevance electrical balance-of-plant candidate because it has explicit data-center megaproject order disclosure tied to medium-voltage switchgear and AI/data-center power demand.

MOD should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a thermal balance-of-plant candidate because its SEC filing explicitly links data-center cooling demand to AI/HPC-driven heat loads and hybrid/liquid cooling.

BELFB is a speculative-shadow candidate: market cap and obscurity fit the underfollowed lens, but later layers must verify material AI/data-center revenue, design wins, and whether power-conversion components are supply constrained.

For this node, the strongest early evidence appears in companies disclosing backlog, megaproject bookings, data-center cooling capacity, or explicit AI/HPC heat-load commentary rather than generic electrification language.

Next Layer 1B pass should separately test nVent, IES Holdings, Atkore, Flex/JetCool, Trane/LiquidStack, and Hammond Power Solutions/OTC availability for busway, cable management, installation, CDU, and transformer exposure.

summary: Layer 1B expansion for the AI data-center electrical/thermal balance-of-plant node. The reference lane is represented by Vertiv as the obvious pure-play anchor in critical power, cooling, monitoring, and services. The underfollowed lane emphasizes less-obvious US-listed suppliers where AI data-center demand may appear through medium-voltage switchgear, engineered power distribution, thermal systems, liquid-cooling capacity, and smaller power-conversion components rather than through headline semiconductor exposure. This is a research universe expansion only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
